text: BESC 201 Introduction to Bioenvironmental Sciences Credits: 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Overview: 3 Lecture Hours. A broad survey of environmental science with an emphasis on scientific literacy, current events, global and international issues and historic context.

BESC 203 Microbiomes and Their Environment Credits: 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Overview: 3 Lecture Hours. Fundamentals of microbiomes; emphasis of interactions between microbiomes and their environments; assessment of impacts of microbiome functions on human, animals, plants and environmental processes; consideration of social and legal implications of microbiome engineering.

BESC 204 Molds and Mushrooms: The Impact of Fungi on Society and the Environment Credits: 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Overview: 3 Lecture Hours. Introduction to the fungi and the impact these organisms have on society and the environment; includes life cycles of fungi; classification schemes, pathogens of plants, animals and humans, fungi in food production; toxic fungi and the law, and others.

text: BESC 367 U.S. Environmental Regulations Credits: 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Overview: 3 Lecture Hours. Investigation of the legal infrastructure of the U.S. associated with regulating environmental impacts; examination of major U.S. environmental statutes associated with air and water quality, toxic substances, waste and hazardous substance release, energy and natural resources; review the relationship between U.S. policy and international environmental regulations. Prerequisites: BESC 201 , ENSS 105 or RWFM 308 . Prerequisite: BESC 201 , ENSS 105 or RWFM 308.

Metabolic pathways of microbes involved in the biodegradation of hazardous materials; ecological requirements for biotreatability of contaminated sites; emphasis on factors affecting microbial growth; strategies for in situ bioaugmentation.
